instruction: In the spreadsheet, identify the top 5 highest marks in the "Marks" column and apply yellow highlighting to these cells. Make sure to only highlight the marks themselves in column C, not the entire row.

metadata.explanation: Task requires identifying top 5 marks and applying yellow highlighting. Top 5 marks by position are [95.0, 89.0, 76.0, 74.0, 74.0] (note two cells have 74.0). Evaluator verifies that the top 5 cells have yellow fill color applied, checking both the fill color RGB value and that only the correct cells are highlighted.

llm_judge_reasons: Getter correctly extracts fill color RGB values from column C cells (lines 31-44), including normalization to handle 'FF' prefix variants
Metric correctly verifies yellow highlighting specifically by checking fill_color against yellow_colors array (lines 21, 35-36), not just any fill color
Metric properly sorts cells by value descending and takes top N positions (lines 24, 27), correctly handling the top 5 requirement
Metric penalizes incorrectly highlighted cells outside top N (lines 42-45), ensuring only top marks are highlighted

Minor issue: expected_top_values contains 4 values [95.0, 89.0, 76.0, 74.0] when top_n=5, but this works correctly because the 5th cell (74.0) is already in the list due to duplicate. The logic 'cell[value] in expected_top_values' handles this properly.
Postconfig appropriately saves the file (Ctrl+S) before evaluation to ensure formatting changes are persisted
llm_judge_fix_suggestions: Optional improvement: Update expected_top_values to explicitly list all 5 values including the duplicate: [95.0, 89.0, 76.0, 74.0, 74.0] for better clarity, though current implementation works correctly
